issues.description: Duplicate "transcriber_error" literal in the message_type tuple is redundant.
issues.detail: The tuple membership test lists "transcriber_error" twice. Set semantics make the second entry inert, but it signals the author did not read what they wrote. A reader auditing the error taxonomy will pause on this. Deduplicate, and consider a module-level frozenset constant so the set is constructed once and named.

issues.description: Loop invariant of _receive_messages is now implicit and undocumented.
issues.detail: After the refactor, _receive_messages is an async for that swallows per-message exceptions and exits silently when the iterator terminates. The invariant ("on normal close, return so the outer reconnect loop drives recovery; on per-message parse failures, log and continue") should be stated in a docstring comment. Future readers will otherwise re-derive it under pressure.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except may now propagate websocket exceptions instead of terminating cleanly.
issues.detail: The PR description argues the old try/except caused an infinite reconnect loop. Fair. But the new shape relies on the websocket async iterator raising no exception on disconnect, only StopAsyncIteration. If the underlying library raises ConnectionClosed from __anext__, the exception now escapes _receive_messages uncaught. Audit the iterator contract and state which exceptions terminate the loop vs. propagate.

issues.description: Error-type enumeration is data, not control flow; lift it to a named constant.
issues.detail: A fourteen-element tuple inside an elif branch is a data table masquerading as syntax. Define ELEVENLABS_ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES = frozenset({...}) at module scope with a one-line comment citing the ElevenLabs cookbook URL. The elif then reads "message_type in ELEVENLABS_ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES" and the taxonomy becomes auditable in one place.

issues.description: Lost per-error-type logger.error call reduces diagnostic signal.
issues.detail: The previous code logged each error category at error level with a category-specific prefix before pushing the error frame. The unified branch drops the logger.error entirely; only push_error fires. Operators reading logs will no longer see ElevenLabs error categories at error level. Restore a single logger.error(f"ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}") before push_error.

issues.description: Missing trailing newline in changelog file.
issues.detail: The new changelog/3233.fixed.md ends without a final newline (\ No newline at end of file). Trivial, but POSIX text files end with \n and many tools (cat concatenation, diff, some markdown renderers) misbehave without it. One byte fix; worth doing for the reader.

review.summary: The fix is directionally correct: removing the outer try/except that swallowed websocket-close exceptions stops the infinite reconnect loop, and consolidating the error-type branches collapses repetition. UNDER-AUDITED on the iterator contract: the new shape assumes the websocket async iterator signals disconnect via clean termination rather than a raised exception, and that assumption is not stated. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on _receive_messages — the loop invariant and termination conditions should be in a docstring, not inferred. The error-type tuple is a data table that wants to be a named frozenset constant, with the duplicate \"transcriber_error\" entry removed and the per-category logger.error restored so operators retain diagnostic signal.
